findings.before: Header declares Type=Concepts, Draft V1.0 R0 and Baseline 1.0; no local edition/contribution history. Concepts is outside the adopted uniform Type vocabulary. The received Baseline declaration alone supplies no selection evidence.
findings.proposal: Use Family=Architecture and Type=Architecture for the primary conceptual-definition responsibility. Preserve received V1.0 R0 Draft/Baseline declaration in history without inventing an author or approval event; actual assistant contribution is separately attributed. Working successor remains Draft/Baseline Not assigned. Do not invent Component or Class and retain DF-ARC-003/path.
findings.closure_criterion: Working classification uses the uniform four-Type contract; received edition and actual contribution remain traceable; no inherited approval/Baseline, invented authorship or ID migration.

findings.before: Three untyped diagrams use Knowledge→Documentation→Document→Metadata→Identity→Classification→Relationships→Registry, with Graph appended in §§6/8. Section8 calls this a dependency hierarchy while prose says higher-level concepts depend on lower-level concepts; neither consumer/provider direction, scope nor contract is defined. The diagrams mix representation, description, identity, classification, projection and mandatory dependency.
findings.proposal: Replace each diagram with an explicitly typed view preserving original section provenance. Separate concept/representation associations in §§4/6 from declared required consumer→provider contracts in §8, with contract and scope. Do not infer required edges or execution order from visual position. Reconcile selected intended contracts against Blueprint §8.11 and retain outstanding ARC-004/005/component conflicts; no verified global DAG and no concealed genuine cycle.
findings.closure_criterion: Every view has explicit semantics; every required edge has consumer/provider, contract and scope. Conceptual associations neither masquerade as dependencies nor erase actual required dependencies; full-graph limitations remain explicit.

findings.before: Each document universally has permanent identity, standardized Metadata, classification, explicit relationships and a lifecycle. Metadata is independent from content without qualifying domain ownership, context applicability or coordinated edition evolution; mandatory descriptor interpretation is unspecified.
findings.proposal: Scope normalized-document obligations and explicitly exclude all-location README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md while retaining their content/reference checks. Do not turn explicit relationship support into a mandatory nonempty relationship list for every document. Metadata represents descriptors; Identity/Classification/Governance own domain meanings. Summarize Dictionary definitions, Schema references, Profile constraints and Instance values under one effective Profile. Conceptual separation permits coordinated content/descriptor changes; no catalog or Profile completion is invented.
findings.closure_criterion: No universal normalized header or nonempty relationship requirement for functional files; description/domain authority and applicability are distinct, without fabricated catalog records or guaranteed independent edition evolution.
findings.related_records: INV-02 remains Not applicable; REV2-06; REV2-07; REV2-08; REV2-11

findings.before: Permanent identity and location independence are stated, but the core model never distinguishes logical document, edition, Version, Revision, edition Status and Baseline membership. Classification is generic with no current Family/Type contract or mutable-classification versus stable allocation distinction.
findings.proposal: Add a scoped document/edition distinction without changing existing identity. Domain+Identifier is the logical key; references, Version/Revision, lifecycle Status and membership are associated facts, not alternative keys. Reference adopted stable DF-SSS-NNN corpus allocations independent of mutable Family/Type/location. Summarize uniform four Types, canonical component or admitted documentary-area Family and optional explicitly defined Class; allocation/execution and detailed owner schema reconciliation remain scheduled. Retain applicable numbering-policy references rather than inventing historical editions.
findings.closure_criterion: Document identity, mutable classification, exact edition coordinates, Status and membership are unambiguous across the model. No additional identity key, retroactive edition or allocation/migration is introduced.

findings.before: Registry is called authoritative catalog, Relationships an explicit connection between heterogeneous entities and Graph their semantic network, but the division between authoritative domain records and derived catalog/network projections is absent. The diagrams imply a serial Relationships→Registry→Graph route without declaring whether it is required.
findings.proposal: Relationships owns typed connection records with identified endpoint domains and provenance; relationship kinds distinguish reference, association, replacement, navigation and required dependency. Registry catalog/lookup and Graph semantic-network projections reference exact authoritative records/editions. Derived copies are allowed with current/refresh/stale evidence and do not redefine identity, classification or governance. A Registry-to-Graph data route needs its own scoped evidence rather than a universal dependency assertion.
findings.closure_criterion: Catalog authority is limited to catalog responsibility; typed records and traceable projections remain distinct. No physical single-copy rule, automatic consistency, competing domain authority or universal serial service route is implied.
findings.related_records: REV2-02; earlier Foundation projection closures retain local scope

findings.before: Workflow lists typical states including Published without an applicable transition policy or exact-edition distinction; policies 'ensure' consistency, validation 'ensures' correctness/compliance, and Automation 'performs' activities. Definitions blur framework contracts, actual execution and guaranteed outcomes.
findings.proposal: Keep Workflow/Policies as Governance concepts defining exact-edition state/transition/evidence contracts; label the list illustrative, not a complete current state machine or automatic approval/publication permission. Distinguish DF definitions from applicable DMS/tool/manual execution, with CMS governing changes in its own scope. Validation evaluates identified rules against exact artifacts with result, coverage and limits; it does not guarantee global correctness or approve. Automation capability contracts do not establish an implemented tool, ignore file representations or certify outcomes. Attribution, authorization, review, validation and approval stay separate.
findings.closure_criterion: Definitions describe domain contracts and intended capabilities without claiming unverified execution, universal transition permissions, guaranteed correctness or approval/publication from a validation result.
findings.related_records: REV2-08; REV2-12; earlier exact-edition governance closures retain scope

findings.before: Baseline is an immutable snapshot at a point in time, but no exact member edition selection, approval eligibility, explicit inclusion, independent snapshot identity or pinned relationship context is specified. This allows a path/current version or complete live corpus to be mistaken for the preserved snapshot.
findings.proposal: Define a separately identified immutable, explicitly selected set of exact approved document editions with relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Approval permits eligibility and does not itself prove consistency or membership. A Draft successor does not retarget old members or inherit membership. Selection has a declared scope and need not include every current file/live relation. Preserve the received declaration as evidence; no actual snapshot or approval record is fabricated.
findings.closure_criterion: Baseline member references remain exact and immutable; identity, eligibility, consistency and inclusion are separate, with no automatic current-path retargeting or manufactured snapshot evidence.
findings.related_records: REV2-02; prior Foundation snapshot closures retain local scopes

findings.before: Every concept is said to represent an architectural responsibility; Layers provide services upward while remaining independent, and every specification must derive from this concept list. Concept entities, capability components, structural areas and documentary authority are not distinguished. Section9 describes ARC-005 as implementation of concepts, which may be read as evidence that services/specifications exist.
findings.proposal: Distinguish concepts/entities, capability components, conceptual concerns and structural allocation. Knowledge is subject matter, Preservation cross-cutting; five conceptual concerns and seven structural areas are separate views. Keep Metadata in Documentation and Baselines/Workflow in Governance; component examples are not exhaustive. Reference ARC-004/005 for allocation with their unreconciled six/seven/direction limits. Layer dependency claims need explicit required contracts; shared owner references or peer contracts are not execution order. Section10 maps concepts to applicable specification responsibilities, not complete supplied implementations or a self-sufficient authority replacing domain owners.
findings.closure_criterion: No concept automatically becomes a component/Layer; structural and conceptual views are distinct, primary allocations retained and specification/implementation status qualified. Owner-source references do not create a blanket circular execution dependency or claim global structural reconciliation.

findings.before: Concepts are said to remain valid regardless of implementation/format, evolve slowly and preserve backward compatibility; the conclusion says the model ensures consistency/maintainability. These are unconditional guarantees. Principles §8.2 instead allows explicitly justified breaking changes when necessary.
findings.proposal: Express technology independence, stability, reuse and quality as intended contract properties with applicability and evidence limits. Preserve compatible evolution where feasible; incompatible conceptual changes require justification, impact/consumer mapping, explicit versioning and transition evidence under the adopted policy. New concepts/extensions can affect structural scope; no architecture-free extension, timeless validity or operational quality guarantee.
findings.closure_criterion: Stability/technology independence are bounded goals; compatible and incompatible changes have explicit assessment paths, with no automatic quality, applicability or compatibility guarantee.
findings.related_records: REV2-02; Review Policy §5.2; ARC-002 §8.2 partial comparison

findings.before: Five Architecture IDs appear as plain-text source roles with no operational links or source-evidence limits. Section10 labels conceptual Registry/Workflow/Graph targets 'Component Specification' without establishing supplied dedicated documents; no local history/input hash is recorded.
findings.proposal: Add resolving references to actual Architecture/Foundation/review owners and distinguish model definitions, terminology consultation, structural allocation and detailed specifications. Use real paths/IDs only; mark specification-role examples as conceptual where dedicated sources are absent. Record received/input and actual update history, preserving all section numbers and provenance of three originally unnamed diagrams. Do not claim peer cycles, unseen external specifications or implementations reviewed.
findings.closure_criterion: Actual links resolve to intended declarations; source responsibilities, supplied versus illustrative targets and input/local-history provenance are traceable; peer bytes and numbering preserved.
